meta.description: Year-by-year fantasy football injury impact analysis by position and ADP.

methodology.injury_data_source: All seasons (2016–2025): games missed come from nflverse weekly player stats (which weeks the player actually played), and every counted absence is corroborated by an OFFICIAL designation — a weekly injury-report Out/Doubtful ruling, or a weekly-roster Reserve/Injured (IR/PUP) placement. The weekly roster feed records the week each player moved to IR, so IR stints are dated exactly; when no report row falls inside a stint the body part is recorded as Undisclosed rather than guessed. Seasons before 2016 are excluded: their roster feed records only end-of-season status, their drafted pool is far shallower, and snap coverage is thin. There is no production-based guessing: a player who simply stops appearing without either designation (a benching, holdout, suspension, or release) is not treated as injured. Non-injury reserve (Reserve/COVID-19, Suspended, personal) is excluded by its roster sub-code. The Status field reflects the actual designation (on Reserve/Injured => IR; officially ruled Out => OUT; Questionable-and-inactive => Questionable), not the length of the absence. A stint is season-ending only when the absence runs to the final week. A small set of in-game/preseason IR cases that leave no report row and no roster row are added from hand-verified game logs; 2025 is likewise hand-curated against the completed-season nflverse data.
methodology.adp_data_source: Redraft PPR (12-team, single-QB) consensus ADP for each season (2016–2025), covering QB/RB/WR/TE. Universe depth is similar every season (roughly 420–455 drafted players), so injury rates compare across seasons; injury counts come from the injury source and are independent of pool depth — a larger pool lowers the rate denominator but does not add injuries.
methodology.player_matching: Players are matched by normalized name + season + position. Names are lowercased, punctuation stripped, and suffixes (Jr, Sr, II, III, IV) removed. Injury, ADP and fantasy-point records share one canonical name+position per player so joins are exact (2016–2025 match rate ~100%).
methodology.points_lost_estimation: Expected fantasy points are derived from historical ADP-tier baselines by position (e.g., Elite RBs historically average ~280 pts/season). Estimated points lost = max(expected - actual, 0).
methodology.replacement_value: Replacement baselines (per season): QB (~200–240 pts), RB (~128–158 pts), WR (~146–172 pts), TE (~88–108 pts). Net value lost = max(expected - max(actual, replacement), 0).
methodology.adp_tiers: Elite: ADP 1–24 | Early: ADP 25–60 | Mid: ADP 61–120 | Late: ADP 121–180 | Deep: ADP 181+
methodology.impact_labels: Severe: top-24 ADP, 8+ games missed | Major: top-60 ADP, 5+ games missed | Moderate: top-120 ADP, 3+ games missed | Minor: 1–2 games or late ADP | No ADP Impact: undrafted or ADP 181+
limitations: Fantasy points lost are estimates, not exact — actual season outcomes vary by team context, usage, and matchups.

Expected-points and replacement-level baselines are fixed per-tier / per-position constants (see below), not re-estimated from each season's data; treat points-lost as an approximate, order-of-magnitude figure rather than a precise total.

Expected-points baselines are anchored to 2021 and scaled a flat ~1%/yr, so pre-2021 (and far-future) expected values carry more model uncertainty; replacement baselines before 2021 are extrapolated backward, not directly measured.

Injuries are limited to drafted QB/RB/WR/TE; absences are counted only when an official injury-report (Out/Doubtful) ruling or a weekly-roster Reserve/Injured placement corroborates them, so a genuine injury a player plays through (no missed game) or one never reflected in either feed will not appear.
A small number of in-game/preseason IR stints that leave no report row and no roster row rely on hand-verified overrides; other rare edge cases may be missed.
ADP represents pre-season draft cost; mid-season waiver pickups or FAAB values are not reflected.
Injury data may not capture all minor week-to-week injuries, particularly questionable designations that did not result in missed games.
PPR scoring assumed throughout; non-PPR leagues will see different positional values.
2016–2020 are 16-game seasons and 2021+ are 17-game seasons; games-missed totals are not rescaled, so compare per-season rates rather than raw totals across that boundary.

Games missed are full seasons: the team's playoff games count too (playoff_games_missed; reg_games_missed is the regular season). A player whose team made the playoffs has more games he can miss. Fantasy points lost, impact labels and fantasy-week figures use the regular season only, since season-long leagues don't score the NFL playoffs.
Replacement value assumes a typical 12-team league roster construction.

callouts: RBs typically lead in total injuries, but WR injuries concentrated in elite ADP tiers often create larger aggregate value loss.
Top-24 ADP injuries are the most damaging because they remove premium draft capital from fantasy rosters with limited replacement options.
Late-round injuries (ADP 120+) matter less in absolute value terms unless the player had significantly outperformed their draft cost before injury.
Season-ending injuries to top-60 picks are among the most damaging outcomes in the data, removing premium draft capital that is hard to replace and often swinging playoff races.
Injuries to elite-ADP tight ends carry outsized impact because the positional drop-off at TE is steeper than at other positions, so the replacement options are weaker.
